(1) The 'selected-friend detail panel' does not exist as a panel — the center column's 'IN PARTY · 2' section renders the selected friend (Emberlyn) as a giant raw crown shape, which reads as a missing/placeholder asset, not a designed detail surface with that friend's stats, relationship, or actions. (2) The three mandated primary actions — Add Friend, Invite to Game, Battle — are never presented as clear labeled controls; rows only carry two cryptic icon buttons (a person+ and an ambiguous pencil), and there is no Battle action anywhere. 'Invite' is only implied by the dashed 'Open slot · invite a friend' row. CLARITY & HIERARCHY: The oversized crown hijacks focal priority, so the eye lands on a broken graphic instead of the friend's identity or any action; the selected friend also appears twice (center crown card + right party row) with no clear relationship between the two surfaces. Filter chips (All/Online/In Game/In Party/Idle/Offline) carry no counts and 'In Party' overlaps the right panel's job. The center 'Friends · 14' header duplicates the left profile's '14 FRIENDS' tile. The pencil icon's meaning is unclear. VISUAL SYSTEM & CRAFT: The crown is an unstyled flat cream polygon — a hard craft failure that breaks the otherwise coherent ember-on-plum system. All avatars are the identical orange rounded square with the same generic dot glyph, so no player is distinguishable and 'warm personality' is unmet. Secondary text is low-contrast ('READY TO LAUNCH', italic 'In Party · ready', 'ONLINE' labels). The right panel's first-row arrow icon is unclear, and the Requests panel's second row is clipped at the viewport bottom, suggesting the column doesn't scroll internally. TRADE-OFFS: The center column is doing double duty as both list and (intended) detail panel — fixing it requires choosing one job per surface. Labeled actions in a detail panel are hidden until selection, so they must also be surfaced contextually. Distinct avatars are needed but external images are forbidden, so identity must be generated procedurally in-page.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan that keeps all required content: (1) Replace the broken crown card with a true, compact selected-friend detail panel at the top of the center column — distinct avatar, name, class, level, status, mutual-friends count, last-seen — followed by a labeled action row with clear hierarchy: [Battle] as the primary ember button, [Invite to Game] as secondary, [Add Friend] as ghost; this single change fixes the biggest brief gap and the focal-priority problem. (2) Make the three actions explicit and consistent everywhere: keep the labeled trio in the detail panel, add a contextual 'Invite' on empty party slots and keep Accept/Decline on requests; remove or relabel the ambiguous pencil icon (e.g., 'Note') and ensure a Battle control exists. (3) Give every avatar self-contained procedural identity — per-player accent hue + class sigil glyph + initials inside the same rounded-square frame, with the status dot pinned to a fixed corner and a thin ring — to add warm personality and status legibility without external assets. (4) Restore hierarchy and spacing: shrink the selected card to normal detail height so the friends list reads as a list, add counts to filter chips, drop the redundant center 'Friends · 14' (or change it to a section label), and raise contrast on all secondary/italic status text. (5) Polish craft: if a crest is kept for the selected friend, frame it as a styled emblem with the class sigil rather than a raw shape; clarify the right panel's first-row arrow as a 'you' indicator; make the Requests column scroll internally so rows are never clipped; de-emphasize the left stat-tile labels so the XP bar leads. (6) Add one memorable moment: a subtle ready-pulse on the 3/4 bar and a glowing 'Launch Party' state at 4/4, plus a battle-ready badge on the selected friend when in party. Sequence 1→2 first (brief compliance), then 3→4 (identity + clarity), then 5→6 (finish).
